record.paper_title: Positive and free boundary solutions to singular nonlinear elliptic problems with absorption: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: In the one-dimensional quasilinear problem -( |u'|^{p-2}u')' = f(u) on Ω = (-1,1) with u(±1)=0, under the integrability assumption (B) and in the model case f(u)=λu^β-u^α with -1 < α < β < p-1, is there a unique threshold α* such that there is exactly one solution for α in (-1, α*] and exactly two solutions for α in (α*, -1/p + 1)?

evidence.quote: We consider now the one-dimensional quasilinear boundary value problem -( |u'| ^{p-2}u')' = f(u) in Ω = (-1,1), u(±1)=0.
It is reasonable to guess that there should be a unique α* such that there is only one solution on (-1, α*] and two on (α*,-1/p+1). We were unable to prove that this happens in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p>1 and consider the one-dimensional quasilinear Dirichlet problem

   -(|u'(x)|^{p-2} u'(x))' = f(u(x)),  x ∈ Ω = (-1,1),   u(-1) = u(1) = 0,

for positive solutions u ∈ C^1([-1,1]) with |u'|^{p-2}u' ∈ C^1([-1,1]). Assume the standard integrability/regularity condition that f: [0,∞) → ℝ is continuous, that there exists s_0>0 with f(s)>0 for 0<s<s_0, and that the primitive F(s) = ∫_0^s f(t) dt satisfies the integrability requirement

   ∫_0^{s_0} ds / (F(s_0) - F(s))^{1/p} < ∞,

ensuring well-posedness of the time-map associated with the equation.

Specialize to the model nonlinearity

   f(u) = λ u^β − u^α,    with parameters λ > 0 and exponents satisfying −1 < α < β < p − 1.

For each fixed β ∈ (−1, p−1) and each α ∈ (−1, β), let N(α, β, λ) denote the number of positive classical solutions of the boundary value problem above.

Prove or disprove: there exists a unique threshold value α* = α*(β, p) ∈ (−1, −1/p + 1) such that, for some appropriately chosen λ (or for the bifurcation diagram in λ at the natural turning value), one has

   • exactly one positive solution when α ∈ (−1, α*], and
   • exactly two positive solutions when α ∈ (α*, −1/p + 1).

Equivalently, establish that the transition from uniqueness to exactly two positive solutions, as α increases through (−1, −1/p + 1), occurs at a single sharp threshold α*.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit conjecture/open problem in the source overview ("we were unable to prove that this happens in general"). A targeted web search did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving the existence of a unique threshold α* for this one-dimensional p-Laplacian model with f(u)=λu^β−u^α in the stated regime, so it appears to remain open.
